AIRPORT-ENTRANCE.description: Airportway ends here in a huge loop past the terminal buildings of Rockvil International Airport. The main terminal building can be entered to the north, and the road leads southwest back toward the city.

ALLEY.description: This long, narrow, dim alley is flanked by tall, featureless walls. The alley, which begins to the west, ends east of here at a back doorway, through which loud, raucous music can be heard.

AQUARIUM-UNDERPASS.description: You are on Aquarium Drive where it passes under the old elevated highway that runs through the city. To the east is the north side of town, and to the west are the suburbs.

BASE-GATE.description: This is the entrance gate to the Manville Border Security Force Base. The base road continues northwest into the base and southeast away from it.

BOOKSTORE.description: A less likely place for a bookstore you couldn't imagine. This one seems to be stocked mostly with used books. Closely-placed shelves, filled with old books, rise to ceiling, and a pleasant, papery odor fills the shop. The front door leads west.| The proprietor smiles at you kindly.

BURNED-OUT-AREA.description: You are in a tangle of narrow streets. All the buildings around you are deserted, their windows broken, their fixtures looted. Many are no more than burned-out shells. One street, slightly wider than the rest, leads southeast.

CENTRE-AND-KENNEDY.description: At this intersection, Centre Street cuts across Kennedy Street from northeast to southwest. A tall hotel has entrances to the east and southeast. The austere facade of Huang Hall rises to the west. Kennedy Street continues north and south.

COLONIAL-HOTEL.description: This old hotel features many of the architectural luxuries rarely seen nowadays, most notably the huge, multistory atrium. There are exits leading northwest and east.

CONSTRUCTION-SITE-3.description: The Johnson Federal Building, which closed last year when the offices of the few remaining Federal agencies were transferred to City Hall, is being renovated as an office building with commercial space on the ground floor. You can leave the site to the northeast.

CONSTRUCTION-SITE-4.description: A conventional city apartment block is nearing completion here. There are openings in the southeast and northeast corners of the perimeter fence.

DEN.description: A second fireplace fills the far wall of this homey space. Aside from a wall-mounted entertainment center, all the furnishings are gone. An arched doorway leads east.

DINING-ROOM.description: The spacious dining area is flanked by the living room, on the other side of the bamboo curtain to the west, and the kitchen, to the east.

DUMP-ENTRANCE.description: Wicker Drive turns ninety degrees here, leading northeast and northwest. To the southwest is an entrance to the city's primary waste disposal facility, which extends along the southern side of the street. A deserted tenement blocks movement north.

EPILOGUE-BATHROOM.description: An antique, tile decor masks the ultramodern features of this large bathroom. A whirlpool tub fills the far end of the room. The exit, up a few steps, is northeast.

EPILOGUE-KITCHEN.description: Rimmed with butcher-block counters, softly lit by recessed zyolights, and decorated in a random pattern of pastel tile, the kitchen is both lovely and functional. You can exit to the west.

EPILOGUE-LIVING-ROOM.description: Sunken, comfy pillowseats form a vaguely oval perimeter around a central circular fireplace. The rest of the furniture has been removed. The dining room lies beyond a bamboo screen to the east. An open, curving stair leads up to the master bedroom, and a foyer leads north.

FACTORY-ENTRANCE.description: You are on Wicker Drive, which runs northeast to southwest. An alley forks off to the east. A large factory complex can be entered to the southeast, and a gun shop is north of here. A row of tenements stretches off to the northwest and west.

FOYER.description: This bright, airy hallway runs northwards from the living room to the apartment door. Tall, arched entrances lead east and west, and the bath is down a few steps to the southwest.

GUEST-ROOM.description: This is a sunny, cozy bedroom, barren of furniture. The only way out is to the west.

GUN-SHOP.description: You are in a small armaments store, with metal bars over the counter separating you from the proprietor. There is an exit to the south.

INDUSTRIAL-PARK-DRIVE.description: You are on a narrow road circling through a grouping of warehouses and light factories. There are buildings on every side except southeast, where the road leads out of the park.

INDUSTRIAL-PARK-ENTRANCE.description: You are on Wicker Drive, which leads northeast and southwest. A road leads northwest into Rockvil Industrial Park. An old, gray warehouse stands on the northern corner, and an ugly tenement is just east of here.

INTERCHANGE.description: This is a huge cloverleaf interchange which once carried traffic on and off the interstate. The highway lies north, south and west of here, and Halley Drive runs off to the east.

JAIL-CELL.description: You are in a featureless, grimy jail cell. A heavy metal door forms the eastern wall of the cell.

LAUNDROMAT.description: This laundromat is equipped with a vibramat as well as the traditional washers and dryers. The exit is east.

LIQUOR-STORE.description: This is a small establishment stocked with cheap scotch and other liquor. There is an exit to the north.

MASTER-BEDROOM.description: This is a huge, round bedroom, encircled by windows. A stairway leads down to the living room. As elsewhere, the furniture has been removed.

PARK-UNDERPASS.description: At this point, the old, rarely-used interstate crosses over Park Street. The northern suburbs lie to the west, and east of here the street climbs a hill toward a water tower.

PICKFORD-THEATRE.description: This building is the last survivor of the fine old theatres of Rockvil's theatre district. The exit to River Street is to the west.

POWER-STATION-ENTRANCE.description: You are on River Street at the entrance of a utility station which lies to the south. The street continues southeast towards the River Street Bridge. Northeast of here is the entrance to a huge factory complex, and tenements line the street to the west and southwest.

RIVER-AND-PARK.description: River Street, off to the east, ends here at Park Street, which curves from the south to the northwest. A stadium skycar lot is on the west side of Park, and some sort of athletic field is to the southeast. All along the north side of River Street is a vast expanse of placid water, Rockvil Reservoir.

RIVERSIDE-PARK.description: This is the city's most popular park. From the hilltop is a beautiful view of the river as it bends off to the east. Paths to various exits lead north, northwest, west, and southwest.

ROW-HOUSES.description: You are standing just inside the front door of a row of renovated old brick three-story apartments. The inner door leads south, and Southway is just outside to the north.

SERVICE-STATION.description: This is an unusually large skycar service center, where people can bring their cars for a quick battery replacement, scheduled maintenance, or minor repairs. The exit to the street is southeast.

SIMONS.description: This expensive four-star restaurant is a favorite after-theatre dining spot. You can leave to the southwest.

SKYCAB.description: This skycab is a luxurious, top-of-the-line model, a veritable sky limousine. The opulent features include reclining seats, tinted zero-glare windows, and a two-meter viewscreen.

SKYCAR-LOT-1.description: This is a car lot for the Foodville to the northeast. The exit is northwest. An industrial park is visible beyond the fence that borders the rear of the lot to the south and east.

SKYCAR-LOT-2.description: This large car lot serves Rockvil Mall, which lies to the north. There are exits from the lot to the southeast and southwest.

SKYCAR-LOT-7.description: You are in a parking lot with entrances to buildings to the east, west and south. The exit to the street is northeast.

SOLARIUM.description: This enclosed sunporch of your penthouse apartment is surrounded by an outdoor patio, accessible to the south. To the north is a sprawling living room.

STOCK-EXCHANGE.description: This aging, impressive structure was once the economic center for the quad-state region (the Dakotas, Wyoming and Montana). However, in this day and age of decentralization made possible by electronic communications, the activity here is reduced in both quantity and importance. Much of the building has been converted to office space. Wide steel portals lead southeast and southwest.

STUDENT-UNION.description: You are standing in the lobby of a wide sprawling building containing a cafeteria, a bookstore, an auditorium, and offices for student activities. The street is southwest of here.

SYMPHONY-ENTRANCE.description: Airportway curves northeast along the river toward the airport, and a road leads north into the military base. On the south side of the street is Symphony Hall, and next to it is a car lot.

SYMPHONY-HALL.description: This is the home of the Rockvil Symphony Orchestra. An exterior balcony offers a fine view of the river to the east. There are exits to the southeast, south, west, and north.

VELDRAN-HOTEL.description: This high-rise luxury hotel is frequented by business travellers attending conventions at Huang Hall across the street. The exit from the lobby is to the northwest.

ZOO-ENTRANCE.description: You are on Aquarium Drive, where a road branches off to the south into the zoo. To the west, the Drive passes under the old interstate. North of here is the entrance to a stadium skycar lot.
